purpose: Paired Native-vs-MAF evaluation of Durable Verified Success on the frozen 29-task suite

supersedes.reason: Protocol v1 pre-registered the experiment design and validated its plumbing only against mock/dry-run executors; it defined no real BenchmarkExecutor for either arm, so no scoring run could actually execute. Protocol v2 adds real-provider execution plumbing and provenance/cost capture only -- see EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL_V2.md. No experimental parameter changed.

NATIVE.description: The coding agent running in its ordinary execution mode with no MAF orchestration or intervention. Its own execution artifact is still graded by the same independent, controller-side verification pipeline used for MAF.

realExecution.participantAdapter: src/infrastructure/claude-code-adapter.ts (ClaudeCodeAdapter), promptPreamble overridden to empty so no MAF framing text is sent

MAF.description: The same coding agent running under the MAF adaptive mode controller (src/domain/mode-controller.ts) with control/assurance behavior enabled: adaptive STRICT/GUIDED/SOLO_NATIVE mode transitions driven by runtime signals, and controller-side independent verification after execution.

treatmentPolicy.note: Frozen policy dimensions for Protocol v1, unchanged in v2. Runtime mode transitions the controller makes within this policy are adaptive by design (see EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 6); the POLICY governing those transitions is what is frozen here, not any single run's transitions.
treatmentPolicy.interventionPolicy: AdaptiveModeController default policy (src/domain/mode-controller.ts), unmodified for this protocol
treatmentPolicy.contextStrategy: LocalRepositoryIndex (src/infrastructure/project-brain.ts) + EvidenceRuntimeSignalCollector (src/application/runtime-signal-collector.ts) default configuration, unmodified; scoped to file-listing context only, without the full ContextBuilder/ProjectBrain knowledge-base stack RunService uses in the general MAF runtime -- see EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL_V2.md 'MAF context scoping'
treatmentPolicy.retryPolicy: One bounded recovery retry (matching RunService's own defaultRecoveryPolicy.maxRecoveryAttempts = 1) and ONLY when the attempt classifies as PROVIDER_FAILURE from structured evidence (evaluation/experiments/real/lib/session-outcome.ts). A participant task failure, auth/configuration failure, bare nonzero exit, signal termination, timeout or cancellation is never auto-retried. Every retry is additionally gated by the run ledger's invocation ceiling, remaining run budget and remaining run deadline, checked before any process is created. Retries are counted from attempts actually authorized and started.
treatmentPolicy.verificationPolicy: Controller-side CuratorIndependentVerifier (src/evaluation/curator-verifier.ts): hidden grader + SMOKE regression, run after participant execution, never observed by the participant
treatmentPolicy.escalation: STRICT -> GUIDED -> SOLO_NATIVE per AdaptiveModeController transition rules; no manual escalation for this protocol. Enforcement limitation disclosed in EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL_V2.md: the Claude Code CLI runs one non-interactive invocation per session (livePolicyUpdate=false, safeSessionRestart=false), so a decided transition is recorded as DEFERRED_BOUNDARY evidence but cannot be enforced on an already-running session.
treatmentPolicy.recoveryBehavior: src/domain/recovery.ts classifyFailure-driven provider-transient handling only; no additional MAF-side recovery beyond what the adapter itself reports
treatmentPolicy.modelRouting: NONE — same frontier model and effort as NATIVE for every paired run
treatmentPolicy.sandboxing: Same controller-owned, per-run temporary workspace and execution environment as NATIVE
treatmentPolicy.costControls: src/domain/budget.ts HARD allocation mode at the frozen per-run budget ceiling below; no separate MAF-only budget

modelConfiguration.note: Same model/version/effort used for both NATIVE and MAF_ADAPTIVE arms of every paired run. Resolved per the mission header (MODEL: Claude Sonnet 5, Effort: High). Unchanged from v1.

resolution.resolutionSource: Claude Code CLI stream-json assistant message `message.model`, when the CLI reports one
resolution.resolvedModelStatus: Recorded per run as RESOLVED (a concrete identifier distinct from the alias was observed), ALIAS_ONLY (only the requested alias is known), PLACEHOLDER_OR_SYNTHETIC (the provider reported a stand-in such as <synthetic>, which is preserved verbatim but never treated as resolved provenance and blocks a successful real-provider preflight), or NOT_REPORTED. Never invented.
resolution.effortEnforcement: The requested effort is emitted as a real --effort CLI argument (src/infrastructure/claude-code-adapter.ts ClaudeCodeConfig.effort) and provenance records effortArgumentEmitted, so the controlled variable is enforced rather than merely declared.

runCountRationale: 29 tasks x 2 arms x 3 repetitions = 174 participant runs. Unchanged from v1 -- see EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 15.
timeoutRationale: 30 minutes per participant RUN, shared across every attempt of that run rather than granted afresh per attempt. Value unchanged from v1. A controller-owned run deadline is fixed at run start (evaluation/experiments/real/lib/run-ledger.ts); each attempt receives only the remaining time, and an attempt is refused outright when too little remains. evaluation/experiments/real/lib/agent-session-runner.ts races the participant's event stream against that per-attempt ceiling and classifies the run TIMEOUT (cancelling the session) rather than relying on any implicit CLI-side timeout.

budget.note: Same $8.00/run HARD ceiling as v1, applied PER RUN across all attempts rather than per attempt. Each attempt's --max-budget-usd is set to the remaining run budget (evaluation/experiments/real/lib/run-ledger.ts), so a retry can never receive a fresh full ceiling; a retry is refused when too little remains, and refused outright when a prior attempt's cost was unmeasured (fail closed rather than spend against an unknown remainder). Enforcement limitations remain disclosed in evaluation/experiments/real/lib/budget-guard.ts and EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL_V2.md section 8: the controller relies on the CLI's own internal accounting within an attempt and performs a non-blocking post-hoc comparison afterwards; controllerEnforcesRealTimeCutoff stays false. What the controller now guarantees is that the SUM of attempts cannot knowingly exceed the frozen per-run ceiling.

randomization.method: xmur3-seeded mulberry32 Fisher-Yates shuffle of the frozen 29 task IDs; arm order derived from shuffled-position parity (even index = NATIVE_FIRST, odd index = MAF_FIRST)
randomization.note: Reuses the exact v1 randomization.json unchanged -- not regenerated for v2. See evaluation/experiments/validate-manifest-v2.mjs.

invalidRunPolicy.definition: evaluation/protocol.json invalidRuns semantics, unmodified: invalid runs never count as DVS and are reported separately from the valid-run denominator
invalidRunPolicy.modelArmFailure: An arm failure the participant itself caused (task not attempted correctly, candidate produced but grader FAILs, participant crashes on its own logic) is a valid run with a non-DVS outcome; it is never rerun
invalidRunPolicy.infrastructureFailure: executionStatus in {INFRA_FAILURE, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED, QUOTA_EXHAUSTED} or a providerError/infrastructureError present, per src/evaluation/types.ts isInfrastructureFailure
invalidRunPolicy.rerunPermitted: Only for runs classified as EXPERIMENT_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE (provider outage, quota exhaustion, tool/workspace/runner crash unrelated to either arm's own behavior); never for an ordinary arm failure

stoppingRule.description: Run the fixed N=3 repetitions for every one of the 29 tasks x 2 arms; do not stop early because an aggregate trend appears in either direction
exceptions: safety or integrity failure (leakage, nondeterminism, private-material exposure) — stop the affected task or the whole run per EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md section 20
provider outage exceeding a reasonable retry window

contaminationRule: After scoring begins, the benchmark suite, graders, MAF policy, Native configuration, model/version, effort, timeout, task prompts, run count, and statistical plan are frozen. A material defect found mid-run stops the affected experiment and is recorded as an incident rather than silently patched; a benchmark defect produces a suite v2, a protocol defect produces a protocol v2 (this document).

realPreflight.taskSource: evaluation/experiments/real/fixtures/preflight-phase (synthetic, not part of the frozen 29-task suite)
realPreflight.defaultBehavior: Validates manifest/config and frozen tags; resolves ONE Claude Code executable and captures its version; checks `claude auth status` on that same executable; verifies no ANTHROPIC_* routing or credential is forwarded to the participant; builds the synthetic controller-owned workspaces; constructs the real Native and MAF executors and the independent verifier; prints the planned executions; and stops before any provider invocation. No step makes a model call. Prints READY_FOR_BILLED_PREFLIGHT only when every gate passes, otherwise PREFLIGHT_ENVIRONMENT_REPAIR_REQUIRED.
realPreflight.billedBehavior: Re-checks the same gates and refuses to spend if any are unmet, then executes exactly 1 synthetic NON_SCORING Native run and 1 synthetic NON_SCORING MAF run against the preflight fixture only -- never a frozen Phase B/C task.
realPreflight.scope: 1 NATIVE run + 1 MAF run against evaluation/experiments/real/fixtures/preflight-phase/preflight-task only
realPreflight.providerInvocationCeiling: maxProviderInvocations = 1 per arm and maxRecoveryAttempts = 0, enforced by evaluation/experiments/real/lib/run-ledger.ts BEFORE any process is created. A second invocation for either arm is blocked at the ledger, not merely reported afterwards. The report exposes providerInvocations.{allowedPerArm,attempted,started,refused,byArm}.
realPreflight.executablePinning: --claude-path <path> pins the exact executable that is version-checked, auth-checked and then executed, so the binary that was verified is provably the binary that runs.

firstAttempt.outcome: INVALID_BOTH; both arms INFRA_FAILURE with providerError 'agent process exited with code 1'
firstAttempt.note: Preserved unmodified outside the repository as forensic evidence and never rewritten as successful. Its five proven defects (authorization overrun via retry amplification, terminal-state collapse, discarded diagnostics, unenforced effort, placeholder model provenance recorded as RESOLVED) are documented in EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL_V2.md section 15 and repaired on branch repair/protocol-v2-real-runtime-v1.

dryRun.taskSource: evaluation/experiments/dry-run (synthetic, not part of the frozen 29-task suite)
dryRun.note: Unchanged v1 mock-executor plumbing check, preserved as-is; superseded for real-execution verification by realPreflight above.
